prediction.text:
Amazon's 10-K says the 2024 increase in AWS operating income was primarily due to increased sales, decreased payroll and related expenses, and a reduction in depreciation and amortization expense from its change in the estimated useful lives of its servers. Higher spending on technology infrastructure to support AWS growth partly offset these. AWS sales rose 19%, which management tied to increased customer usage, partly offset by pricing changes from long-term customer contracts. For company-wide context, consolidated operating income rose about 86.1%, from $36.85 billion to $68.59 billion, an increase of about $31.74 billion.
Amazon said the increase in AWS operating income in 2024 was primarily due to increased sales, decreased payroll and related expenses, and a reduction in depreciation and amortization expense from its change in the estimated useful lives of its servers. These were partially offset by spending on technology infrastructure, primarily driven by additional investments to support AWS business growth.
Amazon stated that AWS sales increased 19% in 2024, and that the growth primarily reflects increased customer usage, partially offset by pricing changes primarily driven by long-term customer contracts.
At the company level, Amazon attributed higher technology and infrastructure costs in 2024 to increased infrastructure spending, partially offset by decreased payroll and related costs and lower depreciation and amortization from the change in the estimated useful life of servers. These costs are allocated to segments based on usage.
Context (consolidated, not AWS): Amazon's total operating income grew about 86.1% from FY2023 to FY2024.
Context (consolidated, not AWS): Amazon's total operating income rose by about $31.74 billion, from $36.85 billion in FY2023 to $68.59 billion in FY2024.

caveats: The filing does not quantify each AWS driver (sales, payroll, depreciation, infrastructure spend) in dollars, so their relative sizes cannot be ranked.
AWS segment operating income dollar figures were not available as fact records, so no AWS-specific growth calculation is shown.
The consolidated operating income figures are company-wide context and do not measure AWS.
The technology and infrastructure cost passage is company-wide rather than AWS-specific. Amazon says these costs are allocated to segments based on usage.
